subject: Private Offer: EU tax surcharge + reseller margin — coordination
messages:
From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 17:12:00 +0100
Subject: Private offer questions — regional tax and partner margin

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the draft private offer. A couple of items came up in procurement that we need to lock before signature:

- The price schedule shows a line for 'EU regional tax surcharge' (3.5%) — can you confirm whether that is a pass-through tax or a Redwood-managed surcharge? Our legal team wants the mechanism explicitly called out in the PO.

- We work through CloudReseller Ltd in several markets. They expect a minimum reseller margin of 12% on private offers. The draft has a 'channel uplift' but it's not broken out by reseller. Can Redwood provide a channel margin carve-out or confirm list-price adjustments so our reseller can invoice cleanly?

Appreciate quick clarity — procurement is hoping to get this in the signature queue this week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Smith
Director Procurement, AcmeHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — regional tax and partner margin

Alex — thanks for flagging this. Looping in Ben (pricing/finance) and Connor (deal ops) to confirm the preferred routing. Quick answers up front:

- The 'EU regional tax surcharge' in the draft is a line-item intended as a pass-through (we invoice the customer and remit to tax authorities), but the PO language is currently generic. We can change the wording to 'pass-through VAT/regional tax (remitted by Redwood)'.

- For the reseller margin: Redwood doesn't typically invoice the reseller separately, but we can provide a split in the pricing workbook so CloudReseller sees a post-discount margin column. If Acme requires an explicit carve-out on the PO, we'll need to confirm the commercial impact with finance (Ben) and ensure it doesn't affect commit accounting.

Ben/Connor — can you confirm whether a 12% guaranteed margin is acceptable as an internal holdback (i.e., Redwood nets to list price and logs a partner margin in settlement), or if we should model the margin as an explicit line on the PO?

I'll also attach the current PO draft for reference (attached).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer questions — regional tax and partner margin

Marissa / Connor,

Reviewed the draft + Alex's ask. Notes: 

1) EU surcharge: we can keep as pass-through VAT. Please ensure PO language contains 'Customer is responsible for regional taxes and Redwood will remit collected taxes to appropriate authorities; amounts shown are pass-through and not a fee to Redwood.' That keeps accounting clean and avoids revenue recognition ambiguity.

2) Reseller margin (12%): We generally treat partner commissions as a post-revenue settlement (commission) rather than an explicit PO reduction. Operationally that means Redwood invoices Acme at the agreed list, recognizes revenue normally, and then pays CloudReseller a commission per our partner contract.

3) If Acme needs the margin shown on the PO for their internal cost-allocation, we can provide a 'Suggested reseller margin' appendix or an export from channel-pricing-workbook.xlsx that shows: list_price, negotiated_discount, suggested_reseller_margin (12%), and resulting reseller_net_amount. But we don't recommend making the reseller margin an explicit credit line on the Redwood invoice — that creates tax and revenue recognition complications in certain EU jurisdictions.

Action items:
- Marissa: change PO wording for pass-through tax as above.
- Connor: generate the channel-pricing worksheet slice for CloudReseller (by country) and attach. Use the '12% margin' scenario as a starting point.
- Legal/Internal finance: if Acme absolutely requires an invoice-level carve-out, we need to route to legal to draft language that preserves our revenue recognition treatment.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Pricing & Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

Alex / team,

Thanks — attached is the per-country slice for the 12% reseller margin scenario (channel-pricing-workbook.xlsx). A few implementation notes in the sheet:

- Column 'Reseller_Eligible' marks only the countries where CloudReseller has local consent to resell (we excluded a couple of regulated EU markets where reseller arrangements require local contracts).
- 'Suggested_invoicing_text' tab includes a short PO appendix you can paste under 'Special Instructions' in Acme's PO template. It reads: "Redwood invoices list price. Regional taxes shown as pass-through; reseller commissions are settled between Redwood and CloudReseller per partner agreement. For internal cost allocation, the enclosed table shows suggested reseller margin and net amounts."

Note: partners@cloudreseller.com is on copy — if they want a different margin in certain countries we should capture that now.

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround everyone. Final confirmation:

- We'll update the PO language to explicitly call the EU amount a pass-through VAT/regional tax remitted by Redwood.
- We'll not change the Redwood invoice structure (no explicit reseller credit line). Instead we'll provide the attached table (per-country) as a PO appendix so Acme can reflect reseller economics internally.
- If CloudReseller requests a country-specific uplift >12%, please have them reply-all with the country and requested margin; we'll run the delta through Ben for approval and route any wording changes to Irene (legal).

Next steps:
1) Connor will add the 'Suggested reseller margin' appendix to the PO draft and re-upload RDW_PO_Acme_Draft_v1.pdf with the appendix inserted.
2) Ben will sign off on any margin exceptions within 24 hours of a reseller request.
3) Marissa will reconfirm final PO language with Acme procurement and push to signature.

Alex — can you confirm that approach works for Acme and whether procurement still wants the 12% shown directly on the PO (we prefer the appendix approach)?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
